context.name: Context
context.label: Immich in the world
context.blurb: Who uses a self-hosted Immich instance, and the few outside services it reaches for. Almost nothing leaves the box — that is the point of the product.

nodes.name: Photo owner
nodes.desc: Backs up a camera roll, then expects to find a photo by describing it months later. Never has to hand the library to anyone else's cloud.

nodes.name: Administrator
nodes.desc: Runs the box. Pauses queues, re-runs jobs over the whole library, swaps the CLIP model, and watches disk fill up.

nodes.name: Immich
nodes.desc: Stores originals on your own disk, derives thumbnails and embeddings from them, and serves a timeline, a map, people and search over the result.

nodes.name: External library
nodes.desc: A folder of existing photos Immich indexes in place and never moves. Watched with a filesystem watcher plus a nightly scan.

nodes.name: OIDC provider
nodes.desc: Optional single sign-on — Authelia, Keycloak, Authentik. Immich does discovery against the issuer and runs a PKCE authorization-code grant.

nodes.name: SMTP server
nodes.desc: Album invitations, welcome mail, password resets. The only outbound channel to a human who is not already logged in.

nodes.name: Hugging Face Hub
nodes.desc: Where models are fetched from on first use. After the first download the box works with no internet at all.

nodes.name: GitHub releases
nodes.desc: Checked on a schedule so the admin console can say a newer version exists. Switchable off, and the only telemetry-shaped call in the system.

edges.label: indexes in place, watches for changes

containers.name: Containers
containers.label: Inside Immich
containers.blurb: Four containers in the compose file, but five things that run: the API and the job worker are separate Node workers that ship inside one image. Dashed lines are asynchronous.

nodes.name: Mobile app
nodes.desc: Does the actual backing up. Uploads in the background, tracks what it has already sent locally, and holds a websocket open so the timeline updates without a refresh.

nodes.name: Web app
nodes.desc: There is no web container. The API worker serves the built SvelteKit app itself as its fallback route, so the browser and the REST API share one origin.

nodes.name: CLI
nodes.desc: Bulk upload from a shell. Hits the same public REST endpoints as the apps, generated from the same OpenAPI schema.

nodes.name: API worker
nodes.desc: Answers every HTTP request, serves the web app, and owns the cron schedule. It never runs a background job — it only enqueues them.

nodes.name: Job worker
nodes.desc: The 'microservices' worker. Same image and same code as the API, started as a second Node worker; IMMICH_WORKERS_EXCLUDE is all it takes to move it to another machine.

nodes.name: Machine learning
nodes.desc: Stateless inference over HTTP. It has no database credentials and no media volume — every request carries the image bytes and the model settings with it.

nodes.name: Redis
nodes.desc: Two jobs in one. It is the job queue, and it is also the socket.io pub/sub backplane — which is how work finished in the job worker reaches a browser attached to the API worker.

nodes.name: Postgres
nodes.desc: Everything durable, including both vector indexes and the offline place-name table. Also the coordination primitive: advisory locks decide which instance owns the cron schedule.

nodes.name: Media store
nodes.desc: Originals, thumbnails, transcoded video, profile images and backups under one mount. Originals are written once and then only ever read.

nodes.name: OIDC provider
nodes.desc: Optional. Only the API worker talks to it.

nodes.name: SMTP server
nodes.desc: Reached from the notifications queue, never from a request thread.

nodes.name: GitHub releases
nodes.desc: Polled by a scheduled job, not by the API.

jobs.components.name: Job worker
jobs.components.label: Inside the job worker
jobs.components.blurb: One BullMQ worker per queue, and one service that decides what happens next. Nothing to the right of the divide lives in this process.

nodes.name: BullMQ workers
nodes.desc: Eighteen workers, all constructed with concurrency 1 and then re-set at runtime from system config. Changing thumbnail concurrency in the admin UI needs no restart.

nodes.name: JobService
nodes.desc: The whole pipeline is here, and only here. Each handler returns a status and JobService decides what to enqueue next — the services themselves do not know the order.

nodes.name: MetadataService
nodes.desc: Reads exif, then resolves the coordinates to a place name against a table in Postgres. No geocoding API is ever called.

nodes.name: StorageTemplateService
nodes.desc: Renames the original into the user's configured folder template. Only continues the chain when the asset arrived by upload or copy.

nodes.name: MediaService
nodes.desc: Thumbnails, previews and the transcoded video. This is the gate — nothing downstream can run until an asset has a preview image to look at.

nodes.name: SmartInfoService
nodes.desc: Turns the preview into a vector. Re-checks the configured model name after inference and throws the result away if an admin changed it mid-flight.

nodes.name: PersonService
nodes.desc: Two separate queues. Detection finds boxes and embeddings; recognition clusters one face at a time against everything already known.

nodes.name: OcrService
nodes.desc: Pulls readable text out of the preview so screenshots and signs become searchable.

nodes.name: MachineLearningRepo
nodes.desc: Pings every configured ML url on a timer and tries the healthy ones first, then the unhealthy ones anyway. It only fails when every url has failed.

nodes.name: Redis
nodes.desc: Shared queue.

nodes.name: Postgres
nodes.desc: Shared database.

nodes.name: Media store
nodes.desc: Shared mount.

nodes.name: Machine learning
nodes.desc: Another container.

ml.components.name: Machine learning
ml.components.label: Inside the machine learning service
ml.components.blurb: A thin HTTP shell around a model cache. Nothing here is persistent except the ONNX files on disk.

nodes.name: FastAPI app
nodes.desc: Two endpoints that matter. Every request names its own model and options, so the service holds no per-instance configuration of its own.

nodes.name: ModelCache
nodes.desc: Keeps loaded models resident between requests and evicts them after five idle minutes. A background poller does the eviction, so idle memory actually comes back.

nodes.name: InferenceModel.load
nodes.desc: On a cache miss it fetches the model from the Hub if it is not on disk yet, then builds a runtime session for it. First request after a model change is slow; the rest are not.

nodes.name: Thread pool
nodes.desc: Inference is synchronous and CPU-bound, so it runs off the event loop. Without this one slow image would stall every other request.

nodes.name: CLIP models
nodes.desc: Two halves of the same model, loaded independently. Images go through the visual half at upload; search queries go through the textual half.

nodes.name: Facial recognition
nodes.desc: A detector that returns boxes and a recogniser that turns each box into an embedding. One request runs both.

nodes.name: OCR models
nodes.desc: Finds text regions, then reads them. Scores for the two stages are thresholded separately.

nodes.name: ONNX session
nodes.desc: Every model is ONNX, which is why the same image can run on a CPU, an Nvidia GPU or a Raspberry Pi accelerator by changing only the tag.

nodes.name: Job worker
nodes.desc: Another container.

nodes.name: Model cache volume
nodes.desc: The only volume this container mounts. It holds ONNX files and nothing about your photos.

nodes.name: Hugging Face Hub
nodes.desc: Reached once per model, then never again.

cues.title: Upload posted
cues.note: Multipart POST /api/assets with a checksum computed on the phone. If the server already holds that checksum it answers duplicate and the bytes are discarded.

cues.title: Original written
cues.note: Straight to disk under upload/. This is the last time anything writes to the original file; every later stage only reads it.

cues.title: Metadata job queued
cues.note: The request ends here. AssetExtractMetadata goes on the metadataExtraction queue and the phone gets its 201 back.

cues.title: Worker picks it up
cues.note: The job worker drains the queue. Exif is read, and the coordinates become a place name using a table in Postgres — no geocoding API is called.

cues.title: Thumbnails written
cues.note: The file is first moved into the user's folder template, then sharp produces preview and thumbnail plus a thumbhash for the blurred placeholder.

cues.title: Second wave queued
cues.note: Only now, and only for an upload: SmartSearch, AssetDetectFaces and Ocr are queued together, plus AssetEncodeVideo if it is a video.

cues.title: Fan-out runs
cues.note: Three separate queues with independent concurrency. A slow transcode cannot hold up face detection.

cues.title: Embedding requested
cues.note: The preview is read and posted as multipart bytes with the model name attached. The ML container has no access to the media volume at all.

cues.title: Embedding stored
cues.note: Upserted into smart_search, indexed by vchordrq with cosine distance. The photo is searchable by description from this moment.

cues.title: Client event published
cues.note: The job worker has no websocket connections of its own, so it publishes on_upload_success through the socket.io Redis adapter instead.

cues.title: Handed to the socket server
cues.note: The API worker holds the actual connection. The adapter is the only reason a job finishing in one process can reach a browser attached to another.

cues.title: Photo appears
cues.note: Emitted into a room named after the user id, so the event reaches every device that person has open and nobody else.

cues.title: Query submitted
cues.note: POST /api/search/smart with free text like "red bicycle in the snow". This path is entirely synchronous — no queue, no worker.

cues.title: Query encoded
cues.note: The API worker calls the ML service directly. Results are memoised on model name + query + language, so a repeated search skips inference entirely.

cues.title: Nearest neighbours
cues.note: Cosine search over the same smart_search vectors written at upload. vchordrq.probes is set per transaction, trading recall for latency.

cues.title: Results returned
cues.note: Ranked assets, filtered to what this user is allowed to see. The text was never compared to a caption — both sides are vectors.

cues.title: Job delivered
cues.note: One BullMQ worker per queue. Concurrency is applied after construction from system config, so the admin UI can retune it live.

cues.title: Handler dispatched
cues.note: Jobs are routed by decorator — a handler declares its JobName and queue, and startup fails loudly if one is missing.

cues.title: Exif extracted
cues.note: Dates, dimensions, camera, coordinates. The place name comes from geodata_places in Postgres, matched within 500km of a populated place, falling back to country boundaries.

cues.title: Moved into place
cues.note: The original is renamed into the user's folder template. This step only continues the chain when the asset came from an upload or a copy.

cues.title: Preview generated
cues.note: Preview, thumbnail and thumbhash. Everything downstream reads the preview, never the original — which is why this step gates the rest.

cues.title: Fan-out queued
cues.note: Smart search, face detection and OCR queued in one call, plus video transcode for a video. The services being queued know nothing about each other.

cues.title: Second wave delivered
cues.note: Three different queues now, each with its own concurrency and its own pause switch in the admin console.

cues.title: Dispatched again
cues.note: Same dispatch path, different handler. There is no separate pipeline engine — onDone is the whole thing.

cues.title: Embedding requested
cues.note: The preview path is handed over for CLIP encoding.

cues.title: Sent to a healthy server
cues.note: Healthy urls are tried first, then the unhealthy ones anyway, and only an all-url failure throws. A /ping check on a timer maintains the health map.

cues.title: Embedding upserted
cues.note: The configured model name is re-read after inference — if an admin swapped models mid-job the result is discarded rather than mixed into the index.

flows.name: A face waits for a crowd

cues.title: Recognition delivered
cues.note: One job per detected face on the facialRecognition queue. Detection already ran and wrote the embeddings; this step only clusters.

cues.title: Dispatched
cues.note: A face that already has a person is skipped immediately, so re-running the queue over a whole library is cheap.

cues.title: Neighbours looked up
cues.note: The face's embedding is searched against every other face this user owns, bounded by maxDistance.

cues.title: Vector search runs
cues.note: A separate vchordrq index from smart search, with its own probes setting. Matches are also filtered by birth date so a person cannot be matched to photos predating them.

cues.title: Deferred, not discarded
cues.note: Fewer than minFaces matches means this is not yet a core face. Rather than inventing a person, the job is re-queued with deferred: true and drops to the back.

cues.title: Second attempt
cues.note: By the time the deferred job runs, other faces from the same batch have been clustered — so the crowd it needed may now exist.

cues.title: Dispatched again
cues.note: Same handler, this time with the deferred flag set, which disables the defer branch. A face is deferred at most once.

cues.title: Matched to a person
cues.note: If any neighbour already belongs to a person, this face joins them. Only a core face with no match at all creates a new unnamed person.

cues.title: Face reassigned
cues.note: The face row gets its person id. A new person also triggers a thumbnail job, which is why an unnamed face appears in the People tab within seconds.
